title: China's crude purchase priority in a highfreight environment
section_path: China's crude purchase priority in a highfreight environment
section_path_text: China's crude purchase priority in a highfreight environment
summary:
Main
When freight rates surge more dramatically than oil, controlling freight costs becomes increasingly important to refiners' overall feedstock economics. By Emma Li
As China's refinery strategy has shifted towards revenue recovery following Beijing's removal of transportation fuel export restrictions in late June, refiners - particularly state-run oil majors that still have substantial unused fuel export quotas - are increasingly prioritising crude cost control rather than simply maximising crude imports. As highlighted in our previous insight [last session] , China's crude demand recovery should be accompanied by a return to baseload Middle Eastern supplies, particularly Saudi and Iraqi medium-to-heavy grades, via relatively short-haul routes through Hormuz.

children.title: China to balance Asian product market with strong Q4 export momentum
section_path: China to balance Asian product market with strong Q4 export momentum
children.section_path_text: China to balance Asian product market with strong Q4 export momentum
children.summary: China's decision to shun Red Sea Arab crude offers was unlikely to have anticipated the subsequent damage to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. Rather, the arrangement appears to have been a concession from Saudi Aramco to retain its largest term buyers, which had reduced their cargo nominations for three consecutive months between June and August.

children.title: Bullish rather than bearish Q4 outlook
section_path: Bullish rather than bearish Q4 outlook
children.section_path_text: Bullish rather than bearish Q4 outlook
children.summary: Q4 still carries considerable uncertainty, with higher crude benchmark prices, firmer spot premiums and elevated freight costs potentially weighing on refinery economics. However, as long as product prices continue to keep pace and refining margins remain positive, Chinese refiners are likely to prioritise utilisation of their remaining annual fuel export quotas.
